hook.situation: A learner can read dictionary forms like 춥다, 듣다, 모르다, and 빨갛다, but the real spoken forms are 추워요, 들어요, 몰라요, and 빨개요. This chapter turns those shape changes into usable habits.
objectives: Match high-frequency dictionary forms with their real polite forms.
Separate true irregular stems from regular lookalikes such as 닫다 and 웃다.
Use irregular forms inside natural sentences about weather, food, health, walking, listening, knowing, and colors.
hook.whyItMatters: If a learner says 춥어요 or 듣어요, the meaning may be understandable, but the sentence immediately sounds broken. Irregulars are not rare grammar trivia; they appear in the first hundred everyday sentences a learner wants to say.

grammarNotes.title: ㅂ Irregular: 춥다 → 추워요
grammarNotes.func: A lot of describing words (and a few action words) whose stem ends in ㅂ change that ㅂ to 우 when a vowel ending comes next. That's why 춥다 (to be cold) becomes 추워요, not 춥어요.

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㅂ, before a vowel ending (-아/어요, -았/었-, -으니까)
formTable.add: ㅂ → 우, then add 어요 (우+어 = 워)

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㅂ, before a consonant ending (-고, -지만, -습니다)

examples.en: The weather is so cold today.
examples.note: 춥다 + 아/어요: ㅂ turns to 우, then 우+어 joins into 워.

examples.en: This bag is really light.
examples.note: 가볍다 follows the same ㅂ → 우 → 워 pattern.

examples.en: My friend helped me with my work.
examples.note: 돕다 is special: ㅂ → 오, so 도+오+아 = 도와요/도와줬어요.

examples.en: Studying Korean is hard but fun.
examples.note: Before a consonant ending (-지만), ㅂ does NOT change: 어렵지만.

keyPoint.label: Vowel ending vs consonant ending
keyPoint.body: The ㅂ only changes before a vowel: 춥다 → 추워요 (vowel) but 춥다 → 춥고 (consonant). Almost all ㅂ-irregular words use 우; only 돕다 and 곱다 use 오. For now, just learn 추워요 as a set phrase and you'll see the pattern.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 추워요 is said smoothly as [추워요]. The 우+어 → 워 is a real spelling change, not just a sound, so you actually write 워.

drill.instruction: Change each ㅂ-irregular dictionary form to the polite -아/어요 form.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: It feels natural to just add the ending and say 춥어요, but ㅂ-irregular stems change the ㅂ to 우 before a vowel, giving 추워요.

grammarNotes.title: ㄷ Irregular: 듣다 → 들어요
grammarNotes.func: A small group of action words whose stem ends in ㄷ change that ㄷ to ㄹ when a vowel ending follows. So 듣다 (to hear/listen) becomes 들어요, not 듣어요.

examples.en: I listen to music a lot.
examples.note: 듣다 + 아/어요: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before the vowel, so 들어요.

examples.en: I walk to school every day.
examples.note: 걷다 (to walk) is ㄷ-irregular: 걷 → 걸 → 걸어요.

examples.en: I asked the teacher a question.
examples.note: 묻다 (to ask) → 물어봤어요; ㄷ → ㄹ before the past-tense vowel.

examples.en: I got a present from my friend.
examples.note: 받다 is a REGULAR ㄷ verb, so ㄷ stays: 받았어요, never 발았어요.

keyPoint.label: Not every ㄷ verb is irregular
keyPoint.body: Only a few verbs change (듣다, 걷다, 묻다 'ask', 싣다 'load'). Everyday verbs like 받다 (get), 닫다 (close), 믿다 (believe) keep their ㄷ: 받아요, 닫아요, 믿어요. You just have to remember which ones are irregular.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 들어요 links as [드러요] — the ㄹ slides into the next syllable. Don't worry about the rule mid-conversation; learn 들어요 as a chunk.

drill.instruction: Conjugate these ㄷ-irregular verbs into the -아/어요 form.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: It's tempting to keep the ㄷ and say 듣어요, but ㄷ-irregular verbs change ㄷ to ㄹ before a vowel ending, giving 들어요.

grammarNotes.title: ㅅ Irregular: 낫다 → 나아요
grammarNotes.func: Some action/describing words whose stem ends in ㅅ drop the ㅅ before a vowel ending — but unlike ㄷ and ㅂ, the two vowels do NOT join up. So 낫다 (to get better) becomes 나아요, keeping both vowels.

formTable.add: ㅅ drops; vowels stay separate (no joining)

examples.en: My cold is all better now.
examples.note: 낫다 → 나았어요; ㅅ drops but 나+았 stays as two parts, no joining.

examples.en: This restaurant is better than that one.
examples.note: 낫다 'be better' → 나아요; the two ㅏ's stay separate, written 나아.

examples.en: Please pour the water into the cup.
examples.note: 붓다 (to pour) → 부어 주세요; ㅅ drops, vowels do not merge.

examples.en: The child laughs loudly.
examples.note: 웃다 is a REGULAR ㅅ verb, so ㅅ stays: 웃어요, never 우어요.

keyPoint.label: ㅅ drops but the vowels stay apart
keyPoint.body: Unlike 추워요 or 들어요, the ㅅ-irregular leaves the two vowels apart: 낫다 → 나아요 (not 나요). Compare regular 웃다 → 웃어요, where the ㅅ stays. The irregular ones to know: 낫다, 붓다, 젓다, 짓다.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 나아요 keeps two clear ㅏ sounds [나아요]; don't shorten it to [나요]. That held, two-beat vowel is the giveaway of the ㅅ-irregular.

drill.instruction: Conjugate these ㅅ-irregular verbs into the -아/어요 form (keep the vowels separate).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners drop the ㅅ and then wrongly squeeze the vowels into 나요. The ㅅ-irregular keeps both vowels: present 나아요, past 나았어요.

grammarNotes.title: 르 Irregular: 모르다 → 몰라요
grammarNotes.func: Words ending in 르 add an extra ㄹ to the syllable before 르 and drop the ㅡ before -아/어. So 모르다 (to not know) becomes 몰라요, with a doubled ㄹ.

formTable.when: 르 stem + vowel ending, when the syllable before 르 has ㅏ or ㅗ
formTable.add: drop ㅡ, add ㄹ to the syllable before, then 라

formTable.when: 르 stem + vowel ending, when the syllable before 르 has any other vowel
formTable.add: drop ㅡ, add ㄹ to the syllable before, then 러

examples.en: I don't really know that person's name.
examples.note: 모르다 → 몰라요; 모 before 르 has ㅗ, so the ending is 라.

examples.en: My friend sang a song.
examples.note: 부르다 → 불렀어요; 부 has ㅜ (not ㅏ/ㅗ), so the ending is 러/렀.

examples.en: Please call a taxi quickly.
examples.note: 부르다 'call' → 불러; same doubled-ㄹ rule with 러.

examples.en: Time goes by so fast.
examples.note: 빠르다 → 빨라요; 빠 has ㅏ, so it takes 라.

keyPoint.label: 라 vs 러 depends on the vowel before 르
keyPoint.body: If the syllable before 르 has ㅏ or ㅗ, use 라 (모르다 → 몰라요, 빠르다 → 빨라요). Otherwise use 러 (부르다 → 불러요, 누르다 → 눌러요). It's the same ㅏ/ㅗ vs everything-else choice as -아요/-어요.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 몰라요 has a strong doubled ㄹ [몰라요] — the first ㄹ closes 몰 and the second opens 라.

drill.instruction: Conjugate these 르-irregular words into the -아/어요 form (watch 라 vs 러).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners try to add the ending straight onto 모르 and get 모르아요. The 르-irregular drops the ㅡ and doubles the ㄹ, so it's 몰라요.

grammarNotes.title: ㅡ Irregular: 바쁘다 → 바빠요
grammarNotes.func: When a stem ends in ㅡ (like 쓰다, 바쁘다), the ㅡ drops out before -아/어. Then the syllable before it decides whether you add 아 or 어. So 바쁘다 (to be busy) becomes 바빠요.

formTable.when: ㅡ stem + vowel ending, when the syllable before ㅡ has ㅏ or ㅗ
ㅡ stem + vowel ending, other vowel (or no syllable before, like 쓰다)

examples.en: I'm so busy these days.
examples.note: 바쁘다 → 바빠요; 바 has ㅏ, so the dropped ㅡ takes 아 → 빠.

examples.en: I'm writing a letter right now.
examples.note: 쓰다 → 써요; nothing before ㅡ, so it defaults to 어 → 써.

examples.en: My younger sibling is really pretty.
examples.note: 예쁘다 → 예뻐요; 예 is not ㅏ/ㅗ, so it takes 어 → 뻐.

examples.en: My head hurts a little.
examples.note: 아프다 → 아파요; 아 has ㅏ, so the dropped ㅡ takes 아 → 파.

keyPoint.label: Drop the ㅡ, then pick 아 or 어
keyPoint.body: The ㅡ always disappears before -아/어. To choose, look at the syllable before it: ㅏ/ㅗ → 아 (바빠요, 아파요), anything else (or nothing) → 어 (써요, 예뻐요). This is the same vowel-harmony idea as regular -아요/-어요.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 바빠요 has a tense ㅃ [바빠요], and 써요 starts with a tense ㅆ [써요]. The dropped ㅡ leaves a strong, double consonant sound.

drill.instruction: Conjugate these ㅡ-irregular words into the -아/어요 form (watch 아 vs 어).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: It feels natural to keep the ㅡ and add the ending, giving 바쁘어요. But ㅡ-stems drop the ㅡ first, so it's 바빠요 (and 쓰다 → 써요, not 쓰어요).

grammarNotes.title: ㅎ Irregular: 빨갛다 → 빨개요
grammarNotes.func: Most color words and a few pointing words (그렇다, 어떻다) end in ㅎ. Before -아/어, the ㅎ drops AND the vowel changes to ㅐ. So 빨갛다 (to be red) becomes 빨개요. Note: 좋다 is regular — 좋아요.

formTable.add: drop ㅎ, vowel becomes ㅐ, add 요

examples.en: The apple is really red.
examples.note: 빨갛다 → 빨개요; ㅎ drops and the vowel turns into ㅐ.

examples.en: The sky is so blue.
examples.note: 파랗다 → 파래요; same ㅎ-drop with the vowel becoming ㅐ.

examples.en: Me too / Same here.
examples.note: 그렇다 → 그래요; a super common one to just memorize.

examples.en: How's the weather?
examples.note: 어떻다 → 어때요; you'll hear 어때요 constantly, so learn it as a set phrase.

keyPoint.label: ㅎ drops and the vowel turns into ㅐ
keyPoint.body: With ㅎ-irregulars, two things happen at once before -아/어: the ㅎ disappears and the vowel becomes ㅐ (빨갛다 → 빨개요, 그렇다 → 그래요). Watch out: 좋다 (be good) is NOT irregular — it's just 좋아요. Learn 그래요 and 어때요 as ready-made phrases first.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 빨개요 is said [빨개요] with the ㅐ vowel; 그래요 is [그래요]. Don't try to keep the ㅎ sound — it's gone before the ending.

drill.instruction: Conjugate these ㅎ-irregular words into the -아/어요 form (ㅎ drops, vowel → ㅐ).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: It seems logical to keep the ㅎ and add 아요, giving 빨갛아요. But ㅎ-irregulars drop the ㅎ and change the vowel to ㅐ, so it's 빨개요. (And don't overcorrect 좋다 — that one really is 좋아요.)

exampleSentence.en: It is easier than I thought.
I listen to music every morning.
I walk in the park after work.
If you do not know, ask the teacher.
I do not know that person's name.
The two colors are a little different.

extendedDialogue.setting: A learner asks why common words change shape in polite speech.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 오늘 너무 추워요. 그런데 왜 '춥어요'가 아니에요?
lines.romanization: oneul neomu chuwoyo. geureonde wae 'chupeoyo'ga anieyo?
lines.en: It is so cold today. But why isn't it '춥어요'?
lines.grammarNote: 춥다 follows the ㅂ irregular, so the natural form is 추워요.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 춥다처럼 ㅂ으로 끝나는 말은 추워요, 더워요처럼 바뀌어요.
lines.romanization: chupdacheoreom bieubeuro kkeutnaneun mareun chuwoyo, deowoyo-cheoreom bakkwieoyo.
lines.en: Words ending in ㅂ, like 춥다, change to forms like 추워요 and 더워요.
lines.grammarNote: The pair is more useful than the label: 춥다/추워요, 덥다/더워요.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그럼 듣다는 들어요, 걷다는 걸어요가 맞죠?
lines.romanization: geureom deutdaneun deureoyo, geotdaneun georeoyoga matjyo?
lines.en: Then 듣다 becomes 들어요, and 걷다 becomes 걸어요, right?
lines.grammarNote: ㄷ changes to ㄹ in common verbs like 듣다 and 걷다.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 맞아요. 모르다는 몰라요, 빨갛다는 빨개요처럼 익히면 돼요.
lines.romanization: majayo. moreudaneun mollayo, ppalgataneun ppalgaeyo-cheoreom ikhimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.en: Right. Learn them as pairs, like 모르다 to 몰라요 and 빨갛다 to 빨개요.
lines.grammarNote: 르 and ㅎ irregulars are easier when memorized through common pairs.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Got it. I will memorize the high-frequency words first.
lines.grammarNote: 알다 keeps ㄹ in 알아요, but drops it in forms like 아세요 and 압니다.

readingText.title: 사전형과 말할 때의 모양
readingText.body: 한국어 사전에는 춥다, 듣다, 모르다처럼 기본형이 나오지만, 실제 대화에서는 추워요, 들어요, 몰라요처럼 바뀐 모양을 더 자주 들어요. 그래서 불규칙 활용은 시험용 표가 아니라 일상 발음과 문장을 바로잡는 도구예요. '오늘 추워요', '음악을 들어요', '저는 잘 몰라요', '이 방법은 어때요?' 같은 문장을 먼저 익히면 규칙 이름도 자연스럽게 따라와요. 단, 비슷하게 생겼다고 모두 바뀌지는 않아요. 듣다는 들어요지만 닫다는 닫아요이고, 낫다는 나아요지만 웃다는 웃어요예요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Korean dictionaries show base forms such as 춥다, 듣다, and 모르다, but real conversation uses changed forms such as 추워요, 들어요, and 몰라요. Irregular conjugation is not just a test table; it repairs everyday pronunciation and sentences. Learn useful sentences first, then attach the rule names. Also remember that lookalikes are not always irregular: 듣다 changes to 들어요, but 닫다 stays 닫아요; 낫다 changes to 나아요, but 웃다 stays 웃어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 사전에는 어떤 모양이 나오지만 실제 대화에서는 어떤 모양을 더 자주 들어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 사전에는 춥다, 듣다, 모르다 같은 기본형이 나오지만 실제 대화에서는 추워요, 들어요, 몰라요 같은 활용형을 더 자주 들어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 듣다와 닫다는 어떻게 달라요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 듣다는 들어요로 바뀌지만 닫다는 닫아요로 그대로 활용해요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 불규칙 활용은 왜 일상 대화에 중요해요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 추워요, 들어요, 몰라요 같은 매우 자주 쓰는 문장에 바로 들어가기 때문이에요.

culturalNote.title: Learn the spoken form, not only the dictionary form
culturalNote.body: Korean learners often study dictionary forms first because that is how apps and dictionaries organize words. Native conversation, however, usually gives you the conjugated shape. If you only memorize 춥다 and 듣다, you may hesitate when you need 추워요 and 들어요. Treat each high-frequency irregular as a pair: dictionary form plus the first sentence you would actually say.
culturalNote.tip: For each new irregular, memorize one real chunk: 추워요, 들어요, 나았어요, 몰라요, 어때요, 아세요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which form correctly conjugates 춥다 in polite present speech?
inlineExercises.explanation: 춥다 follows the ㅂ irregular: ㅂ changes to 우 before 어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which pair shows the ㄷ irregular?
inlineExercises.explanation: 듣다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ. 닫다 and 받다 are regular.
ㅅ drops in 낫다 before a vowel-starting ending.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 르 irregular correctly?
inlineExercises.explanation: 모르다 becomes 몰라요: ㄹ doubles onto the previous syllable.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which form is natural for 어떻다?
inlineExercises.explanation: 어떻다 is a ㅎ irregular adjective: 어떻다 + 어요 → 어때요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence shows ㄹ deletion before -세요?
inlineExercises.explanation: 알다 keeps ㄹ in 알아요 but drops ㄹ before -세요: 아세요.
춥다 describes the weather, so 날씨 takes 가. 를 would make weather an object, which does not fit an adjective sentence.
춥다 is a ㅂ irregular, so ㅂ changes to 워 before 어요. The natural spoken form is 추워요.
모르다 is a 르 irregular and becomes 몰라요. 잘 softens it to “I do not know well.”
걷다 is a ㄷ irregular, so ㄷ changes to ㄹ before 어요. 닫다 is a regular lookalike, but 걷다 becomes 걸어요.

bullets: ㄷ irregular: 듣다→들어요, 걷다→걸어요, but 닫다→닫아요.
ㅅ irregular: 낫다→나아요, 짓다→지어요, but 웃다→웃어요.
ㅎ irregular: 빨갛다→빨개요, 어떻다→어때요, but 좋다→좋아요.

writingTask.prompt: Write 3-4 sentences about today's weather and how you feel, using describing words that are irregular verbs.
writingTask.hint: Conjugate irregulars into 해요체: ㅂ (춥다→추워요, 덥다→더워요, 맵다→매워요), ㄷ (듣다→들어요), ㅡ (바쁘다→바빠요), 르 (모르다→몰라요, 다르다→달라요).
writingTask.model: 오늘은 날씨가 추워요. 요즘 저는 너무 바빠요. 그래서 음악을 들어요. 한국어가 어려워도 답을 몰라도 괜찮아요.
writingTask.modelEn: Today the weather is cold. These days I'm very busy. So I listen to music. Even if Korean is hard and I don't know the answer, it's okay.

canDo: Conjugate 르-irregular and ㅡ-irregular words (모르다→몰라요 · 바쁘다→바빠요)
